bug noun

software

also error, defect, software bug

our formation

mendum, mendī n.

noun, second declension

fault or error

Applied to a software bug.

Examples

  • Mendum est sīcut lapillus quī in calceō tuō latet: nōn bene ambulās, dōnec lapillum invēneris et ējēceris.

    A bug is like a pebble hiding in your shoe: you can’t walk properly until you’ve found the pebble and thrown it out.Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

  • Mendum invēnī.

    I found a bug.composed

  • mendum invenīre / reperīre

    find a bugcomposed

  • vitium invenīre

    find a bug (an earlier alternative)composed

Other words

  • menda, mendae f. — a fault or blemish

    noun, first declension · also used · classical

    A related form.

  • vitium, vitiī n. — defect or fault

    noun, second declension · also used · our formation

    Applied here to software; plural vitia. Our existing preferred everyday “bug” is mendum, mendī n.; keeping that choice makes related phrases consistent.

See also debug, bug report, reproduce a bug, tester.
